implemented.title: Add secret-safe structured Node crash reports

mergedProduct.proof: merged product tree exactly equals the fully tested proposal tree

implemented.capability: opt-in secret-safe structured Node.js crash diagnostics for process targets
implemented.behavior: When target.nodeDiagnosticReport is true for node/node.exe, Ferrum owns Node report flags, writes raw reports only to a temporary directory, retains selected crash/stack/heap/resource/thread and endpoint-free libuv state through EvidenceWriter, records node-diagnostic-report evidence and nodeReports count, and deletes the raw report directory after collection.
implemented.privacy: User report flags that could change the contract are rejected. Retained reports omit raw command line, cwd, hostname, environmentVariables, networkInterfaces, localEndpoint, remoteEndpoint, sharedObjects and other unnecessary host/account detail. Existing recursive EvidenceWriter secret redaction remains in force.
implemented.acceptance: A real uncaught Node exception exits 1, yields one retained report whose JS stack identifies ferrum-node-diagnostic-boom, excludes an injected secret and sensitive host/network fields, and rejects a conflicting user --report-directory before launch.

candidates.head: e148594aaf84d75b2ca14d661988674dfa062f98
candidates.purposeArchitecture: WebdriverIO desktop/mobile service that drives Tauri through embedded WebDriver or provider drivers and exposes Tauri-specific APIs
candidates.harvest: cross-platform driver lifecycle, automatic binary discovery, frontend/backend logs, Tauri API execution, IPC mocking, multiremote and bounded child-process lifecycle
candidates.integrationMode: optional subprocess/driver bridge behind Ferrum's shared target/evidence contract
candidates.expectedBenefit: real Tauri coverage on Windows/Linux/macOS without pretending Tauri is Electron
candidates.requiredDependencies: WebdriverIO Tauri service plus compatible Tauri test build/driver provider
candidates.platformCoverage: Windows, Linux and macOS per current upstream service documentation
candidates.compatibilityRisks: test-build plugins/embedded driver behavior must be isolated from production artifacts; macOS requires a real host to qualify
candidates.upstreamIssues: driver/provider differences and child-process hangs require strict lifecycle timeouts
candidates.benchmarkProductionEvidence: upstream 1.0.0 service and current CI explicitly exercise packaged desktop/mobile tooling and recently added hang backstops
candidates.smallestExperiment: package a minimal Tauri fixture and run launch, semantic interaction, backend IPC/log observation, restart, persistence and evidence capture on Linux and Windows
candidates.acceptanceTest: real packaged Tauri app completes the shared Ferrum lifecycle/evidence contract with deterministic cleanup and no regression to Electron/desktop paths
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: after minimal packaged Tauri fixture is qualified on Linux and Windows

AutomateThePlanet/appium-novawindows-driver versus FlaUI for a native Windows adapter differential
ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp heap query techniques for bounded memory-leak diagnostics
W3C WebDriver BiDi for provider-neutral observability beyond classic WebDriver
rejectedOrSuperseded: appium/appium-windows-driver as the preferred new Windows backend; retain only as legacy compatibility reference

maximumImprovementChallenge.reason: Tauri, native-Windows, BiDi and heap-diagnostic candidates all require new real-runtime fixtures or same-workload comparison before any adapter/dependency can satisfy Ferrum's proven-improvement gate. Adding one now would be speculative architecture churn.
maximumImprovementChallenge.strongestNextExperiment: Build a minimal packaged Tauri fixture and compare direct tauri-driver control with @wdio/tauri-service on Ferrum's existing lifecycle/evidence contract, first on Linux and Windows.
maximumImprovementChallenge.secondaryExperiment: On a real Windows host, compare NovaWindows and FlaUI against the same packaged native fixture for semantic reliability, setup cost, restart/persistence and evidence quality.
maximumImprovementChallenge.diagnosticExperiment: Create a deliberate detached-DOM leak and compare existing Ferrum evidence with a bounded Chrome DevTools heap snapshot/query sidecar.
maximumImprovementChallenge.protocolExperiment: Probe WebDriver BiDi events beside the existing Selenium Grid classic-WebDriver workload without changing its default control path.

guardrails: No new adapter is advertised as supported before a real representative runtime completes launch, interact, observe, failure/recovery where relevant, restart/persistence and evidence capture.
Browser/desktop protocol experiments remain additive until they prove parity plus measurable capability/reliability/agent-efficiency benefit.
Heap diagnostics remain opt-in and bounded; raw evidence stays available and privacy-sensitive host data is not promoted into agent summaries.
No viewport caps, reduced datasets, reduced evidence, reduced target coverage, weaker tests, stale caching or synthetic-only proof may be used to create apparent speedups.
nextResearchCursor: real Tauri adapter fixture, native Windows NovaWindows-versus-FlaUI differential, WebDriver BiDi event parity, bounded browser heap-leak diagnostics, then same-workload agent-browser/rustwright backend benchmarking
